scope: Project-owned source availability and owned output lifecycle contracts from ADR 0036. Independent literal byte vectors test source storage; analytic image oracles and existing compositor controls validate owned rendering.

requirements.status: source storage implemented; complete-source hosted controls pass on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows; document integration remains pending
requirements.gaps: Document parser/cache migration, progressive opening/pages, jobs, protocol and scheduling remain group 11 obligations.
requirements.rule: A source fixes identity and length, admitted against both the configured file cap and target-sized file positions. Supplies validate all overlaps before publishing new fragments. Missing bytes remain separate from terminal errors. Duplicate bytes do not advance availability; conflicting overlap invalidates future reads and cached waits. Every retained allocation stays charged until its last lease drops. Assembly and missing-range frontiers obey explicit caps, and work accumulates across retries. Bounded windows reuse the slice parser, preserve absolute positions, and publish only completed values and diagnostics. An available prefix can complete a unit before later holes; repeated unchanged waits do not reparse. A callback dependency frontier is distinct from incomplete current syntax and terminal failure. Only a frontier of the same immutable source may pause the reader; cursor and provisional diagnostics stay unpublished, and closure takes precedence over a cached dependency wait.

requirements.status: implemented; hosted lifecycle and independent pixel controls pass on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows
requirements.gaps: Protocol, browser/native async adapters and worker scheduling remain group 11 obligations.
requirements.rule: Prepared sessions own scratch, a persistent global-band cursor and preallocated output slots. Pausing never repeats a band. A held immutable lease prevents slot reuse; no free slot means no execution. Cancellation is terminal and leaves existing leases valid and charged. Existing collectors, callbacks and owned sessions share the same executor and exact pixels.

requirements.status: implemented; hosted codec and public render-stream parity controls pass on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows
requirements.gaps: Protocol, CLI and native/browser transport integration remain group 11 obligations.
requirements.rule: PNG emits one canonical zlib stream using fixed DEFLATE and IDAT boundaries independent of input splits or output demand. Admission reserves bounded row/history/token/code/output storage and checks conservative work and output quotas. Pixel rows and output chunks stay bounded; held chunks retain their allocation charge. Only explicit completion after one checksum and IEND signifies success. Cancellation preserves existing leases without producing completion.

requirements.status: owned bootstrap and complete-document admission validated; document materialization and independent stream storage controls implemented
requirements.gaps: Requested-operation opening, partial-document ReadFault propagation and lazy dependency jobs remain pending in the same group.
requirements.rule: An owned opener advances the shared header/tail/xref grammar and revision chain, yielding between completed units and retaining completed sections across exact missing-range waits. It does no work on unchanged waits and charges all window work cumulatively, including failed offset probes. Only explicit complete-source admission and final validation publish one ordinary Document. Structural repair discards the failed primary and invokes the existing full-source reconstruction once, retaining header diagnostics only. Document materialization explicitly returns a shared immutable lease over its source prefix and checks source lifecycle on every call; previously issued leases remain readable after closure. The document retains the admitted immutable lease without copying it; reauthentication and historical prefixes share that allocation and consistency provider. Closure or conflicting supply is checked before cached object, page, stream, historical and render-scene access. Raw stream payloads return source leases; decoded and image payloads retain either the same lease or owned decoded bytes, with no document lifetime or implicit full-source copy. Rendering images retain those leases through scene ownership. Cancellation and terminal failure never publish success; retained lease charges survive producer/source closure until the last owner releases them.
